root_cause: The Drawer component overrides _showElement without implementing autofocus handling. When the drawer dialog is opened via showModal(), the browser focuses the dialog element itself, not the close button. The close button has an autofocus attribute, but the native <dialog> element does not honor autofocus when shown via showModal(), and the Drawer component does not implement autofocus handling in its _showElement override.
repair_strategy: Add autofocus attribute to the close button in the HTML, and modify Drawer._showElement to focus the first element with autofocus after showing the dialog. This ensures keyboard focus moves into the drawer upon opening.

edits.after: <button type="button" class="btn-close" id="filters-close" data-bs-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close" autofocus></button>

expected_accessibility_effect: Upon opening the filters drawer via keyboard (Enter on the Filters button), focus will immediately move to the close button, allowing keyboard users to navigate the dialog without a pointer. Subsequent Tab presses will move focus to the checkboxes and apply button.
functional_risks: If a dialog has multiple autofocus elements, the first one in tree order will receive focus, which may not be the intended target.
If a dialog is opened via a script call that expects focus to remain on the trigger, the autofocus will shift focus. However, this is standard dialog behavior.
The change affects all drawers using this component, but autofocus is opt-in via the attribute.
verification_requirements: After activating the Filters button with Enter, the close button (#filters-close) must receive focus.
Pressing Tab from the close button should move focus to the 'In stock' checkbox.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.
The applied filter text should update to 'in' after pressing Enter on the Apply button.
